- Explored health as physical, mental, and social well-being, not only absence of disease.
- Connected sleep, food, football, talking, fruit, phone use, and relationships with different parts of health.
- Identified that poor sleep and food can affect health even without visiting a doctor.
- Planned breakfast, reducing mobile games to one hour, walking, and sharing feelings.
- Teach-back was not passed; planning effects remained partly incomplete.
end.parentNote: Siya practised viewing health through physical, mental, and social well-being. They connected sleep with mood and memory, football with body and relationships, and talking with mental and social well-being. There was a mix-up when identifying which health effects were clear, and some links were clarified later, though the final routine plan still needed more detail. At home, ask Siya to choose one small daily change and name one physical, mental, and social effect it may have.
